name: Hilton
headline: Collects fees from about 1.3 million hotel rooms it mostly does not own.
what_short: Hotel brands: franchising and management fees
what_it_does: Hilton licenses its brands and manages hotels for owners, earning fees based on a share of room revenue, under contracts of 20 to 30 years. Franchise fees were $2.78 billion and management fees $689M in 2025. It owns only 46 hotels, and its loyalty program is a major source of bookings.
why_it_passed: Management and franchising produced 97% of five-year segment profit.
Operating income was 54% of net tangible assets in 2025, at the top of its field.
The system grew from 1,096,115 rooms in 2022 to 1,336,064 in 2025, with net unit growth of 6.7% in 2025 and a pipeline of 541,300 rooms.
The fee per room kept just ahead of room prices over six years.
why_not_now: The analysis values the shares at $56.50 to $147.79 against a price of $329.59. The best case a buyer could defend returns about 5.7% a year and the central top case 3.1%, against the 5.56% a 30-year US Treasury bond pays.
watch: Debt and finance leases are $13.4 billion, with $4.1 billion maturing in 2030.
Buybacks at $256 to $327 a share were above the top of the analysis's value range and partly borrowed.
Management features adjusted EBITDA in its reports and guidance rather than plain profit.
